part_2_root_cause_independently_confirme.mechanism: A background job launched with & from a non-interactive shell has SIGINT set to SIG_IGN, and an ignored disposition survives exec. The exact-OS child therefore ignored the SIGINT the tests use to drive FAILED attempts; attempts that should have terminated in seconds instead entered the genuine dual replay of roughly 134 plus 133 seconds and post-run control work, overrunning the embedded 300-second budget with empty pipes.
part_2_root_cause_independently_confirme.reviewer_probe: bash -c 'python3 -c "import signal; print(signal.getsignal(signal.SIGINT))" & wait' prints 1, SIG_IGN, while the same command in the foreground prints the default handler. Reproduced on this host during this review.
part_2_root_cause_independently_confirme.explains_everything: All four reviewer executions used nohup with &, so all inherited SIG_IGN and failed identically, including the isolated quiet-host run. The operator's original three runs were foreground and passed. The disagreement was never about the pipeline's speed; it was about who launched it and how.
part_2_root_cause_independently_confirme.reviewer_correction: The BLOCKED review listed the launcher-bytes test as an in-suite error suggesting cross-test interference. Rechecking the original failure summary shows exactly fourteen affected nodes and the launcher test is not among them; the reviewer's dot-position mapping was off by parametrization offsets. The interference claim is withdrawn. In the remediated unified run that test passes in 0.054 seconds after the heavy fixtures.
